positioning: The merry little gun dog who became everyone’s sweetheart.
story: The Cocker Spaniel is the smallest of the sporting dogs and one of the oldest names on the American rolls.

Spaniels came to England from the continent centuries ago and split by job. The smallest were used to flush woodcock from cover. That work gave the Cocker its name. It was one of the first nine breeds recognized in America, in 1878.
In America it took its own path. Breeders here favored a smaller, rounder, more glamorous dog, with a domed head and a long, feathered coat. In time the American Cocker became its own breed.
Then it became a star. By the mid-twentieth century the Cocker was among the most popular dogs in the country. Lady, an animated Cocker, charmed a generation in a beloved film.
The temperament earned the fame. Gentle, merry, and eager to please. A tail that rarely stops. The long ears and silky coat ask for steady grooming.
Beneath the glamour beats a bird dog’s heart. The Cocker still loves to use its nose and please its person.

last_walk:
The string lights come on, and the garden goes quiet.
A Cocker on a bench is a small portrait of patience. Ears like silk, eyes like warm tea. The day’s work is done. The garden has been supervised. All that remains is to sit, be adored, and be glad of it.
